events.title: The martyrdom of St. Oliver Plunkett
events.shortBlurb: The Archbishop of Armagh was hanged at Tyburn on false charges, the last Catholic martyr to die there…
body: Oliver Plunkett, born at Loughcrew in County Meath in 1625, was educated at the Irish College in Rome, ordained in 1654, and appointed Archbishop of Armagh in 1669. Returning to an Ireland ground down by penal laws, he labored, often in hiding and disguise, to reform his clergy and hold the Church together.

In the panic of the fabricated 'Popish Plot' he was arrested in Dublin in December 1679. When no jury in Ireland would convict him, he was carried to London and tried at Westminster Hall in June 1681, where perjured witnesses swore he had plotted a French landing. He was condemned for high treason.

On 1 July 1681 he was hanged, drawn, and quartered at Tyburn, forgiving his enemies and protesting his innocence — the last Catholic martyr to die there. His head is venerated at St. Peter's, Drogheda. Beatified in 1920, he was canonized by Paul VI in 1975, the first new Irish saint in nearly seven hundred years.
